one_month_reasoning: Inside the window: September revenue on Oct 8 (13:30 Taiwan), Q3 results and Q4 guidance on Oct 15, and the FOMC on Oct 27-28 (Fed hiked to 3.75-4.00% on Sep 16 and signalled one more). July+August revenue of NT$982B means September only needs ~NT$450-480B (vs NT$515B in August) to meet the US$44.6-45.8B guide, so a top-end beat is likely but expected. The chain says demand is firm going into the print (N2 orders from Apple/Nvidia/AMD/Qualcomm/MediaTek reportedly up 10-20%, 3nm/2nm/CoWoS still tight per DigiTimes Sep 15, UBS/BofA raising 2027 capex to $85-90B on demand). The swing factors are Q4 GM guidance (N2 and overseas dilution) and early 2027 capex color: a big capex number reads bullish for demand but bearish for FCF, so I do not take a strong directional view. With the stock ~4% below its 52-week high and the 10-year at 5.29%, I keep only a small positive drift (median ~$462, +0.6%) at ~11.8% monthly vol (40%/3.5, slightly widened for earnings), a touch less bullish than round 1.

Stock today ~20.9x FY27 consensus. 72.5% foundry share and pricing power argue for holding ~20x, but the 10-year at 5.29% (highest since 2007) and a hiking Fed argue against expansion, and growth decelerates from 2026's >40%. Cut from 20x in round 1.

Includes a small Taiwan-shock weight.

base.story: FY27 revenue +30-35% on N2 ramp (orders up 10-20%, booked into 2028), AI accelerators/ASICs and likely low-to-mid single-digit price hikes already in consensus; GM mid-60s despite overseas dilution; FY27 EPS ~$22, market pays ~19.5x NTM EPS of ~$25.

bull.story: AI demand keeps outrunning supply into 2028 (UBS 2027 revenue +40%, capex raised to fill orders), price hikes come in at the high end, margins hold ~66%+; FY28 EPS ~$28 at ~23x even with high rates.

thesis_break_reason: $325 (~29% below spot, ~14.8x the $21.93 FY27 consensus, near the March 2026 low area) would most likely mean FY27 estimates are being cut: a real AI-capex pullback visible in Nvidia/Broadcom/hyperscaler guidance, a GM reset below ~58% from the N2/overseas/capex step-up, punitive Section 232 terms beyond the Taiwan carve-out, or a Taiwan Strait escalation, rather than ordinary 40%-vol noise.

reasoning: Round 2. The industry chain is still uniformly strong: TSMC holds 72.5% foundry share; N2 orders from Apple/Nvidia/AMD/Qualcomm/MediaTek are reportedly up 10-20% and booked into 2028; 3nm/2nm/CoWoS are still tight (DigiTimes Sep 15); SEMI projects record $156B equipment spending in 2027 and WSTS +27% chip market growth; UBS and BofA raised 2027 TSMC capex to $90B/$85B on demand. I accept the supervisor's corrections: (1) FY27 consensus is $21.93, not my $22.4; (2) the 3-6% price hike is a single anonymous DigiTimes report (my BigGo/KuCoin cites were recaps), consistent with MS/GS modelling, so I treat it as likely and already in consensus rather than upside; (3) with the 10-year at 5.29% and the Fed hiking, the 22x current-year premium is dropped and the NTM multiple trimmed to 19.5x; (4) capex of ~$88B/105B caps FCF, so I added an FCF-yield leg; (5) Intel 14A/Samsung 2nm claims are colour, not share loss within 12 months. Fair value falls from $515 to ~$473. I stay slightly above the supervisor's $470 because my lane's evidence (order increases, raised capex as a demand signal, rising estimates 9/0) supports FY28 EPS ~$26. The ladder is a lognormal with median ~$483 (fair value plus modest estimate-revision momentum) and sigma 0.345 (down from 0.36, thinning the right tail as suggested; still below 40% realized vol for a mega-cap) mixed with a 5% crash component (median ~$210, sigma 0.35) for a Taiwan or AI-bust tail. That gives P(>=459) 0.53, P(>=551) 0.33, P(>=804) 0.066. Scenario mean ~$487 is consistent. Research in round 2 was 5 searches and 1 fetch (DigiTimes paywalled beyond its headline); no option data or priors were consulted.
